ideas.title: For parents and grandparents
ideas.line: The house that holds the stories.
verse: The front steps where everyone gathered.
The garden they tended, season after season.
The kitchen window, lit for you coming home.
paragraphs: Give it back to them in bricks, for a milestone birthday, an anniversary, or the move to somewhere smaller.

And if they are settling into a new room, in assisted living or a care home, let a little of home go too: a familiar roofline on the windowsill, and a place to begin when you visit. Build it together, a few bags at a time, or let us build it for them.
ideas.think: the family home, their childhood house, a favorite vacation cottage, the house they are moving out of.
ideas.alt: A granddaughter kneels by her grandmother's armchair and hands her a brick model of the family house.

ideas.title: For children and grandchildren
ideas.line: A piece of where they come from.
verse: Grandma’s house, a story in every window.
The farm where every summer began.
The home a grown child takes with them to college.
paragraphs: For the youngest, make it a family project, and share as much of the building as suits them. For the eldest, it is a little piece of home to carry along.
ideas.think: the house they came home to as a baby, Grandma’s house, the family farm, the home they are leaving for college.
ideas.alt: A grandfather and his young grandchild build a brick model of a house together at the kitchen table.

ideas.title: For siblings and the whole family
ideas.line: One place. A dozen versions of the story.
verse: The kitchen everyone remembers differently.
The porch in every summer photograph.
The vacation house where the cousins grew up together.
paragraphs: Give it together: for a reunion, a parent’s birthday, or one last gathering before the house is sold. Choosing the details becomes part of the gift.
ideas.think: the childhood home, a shared summer cottage, the family’s first house in a new country.
ideas.alt: Grown-up siblings and their parents laugh around a brick model of their childhood home.

ideas.title: For a new baby
ideas.line: The home they will grow up in.
verse: The door they were first carried through.
The room where the first steps happened.
The place the christening, or the naming, was held.
paragraphs: A keepsake for the parents, for a birth or a first birthday. It is made of small pieces, so it waits on a high shelf until little hands are ready to help build it.
ideas.think: the house they came home to, the grandparents’ house, the church or chapel of a christening.
ideas.alt: In a sunlit nursery, new parents set a brick model of their house on a high shelf while one cradles their sleeping newborn.

ideas.title: For your partner
ideas.line: Somewhere only the two of you would choose.
verse: The café where an hour felt like a minute.
The first apartment, and its one good window.
The bench, the bridge, the place you said yes.
paragraphs: For an anniversary, or an ordinary Tuesday worth celebrating: build it side by side, and tell the story one more time.
ideas.think: where you met, your first shared home, where you got engaged, a honeymoon hotel.
ideas.alt: On a sofa, one partner surprises the other with a brick model of the seaside cafe where they met.

ideas.title: For newlyweds
verse: The church, the chapel, the barn, the ballroom —
the one room that held everyone they love, at once.
paragraphs: Give it as a wedding gift, or save it for the first anniversary, when the day has become their favorite story. And if you are the one just married, it is a lovely way to say it all again.
ideas.think: the wedding venue, the church where their parents married too, the first home they share.
ideas.alt: A bride and groom hold a brick model of a white chapel as petals fall around them and their guests.

ideas.title: For new homeowners
ideas.line: The first key, kept for good.
verse: A first house. A long-awaited move.
A place to put down roots, and paint the front door.
paragraphs: Celebrate the housewarming, or the first anniversary of the keys, with the home itself in bricks.
ideas.think: a first home, a forever home, the house they built or restored.
ideas.alt: A couple in the doorway of their first home hold up the key, beside a brick model of the same house.

ideas.title: For graduates and lifelong friends
ideas.line: The place that stands for the years.
verse: The residence hall. The library at midnight.
A campus tower like Brown’s Carrie Tower, keeping the hours.
paragraphs: For a graduation or a reunion — or for an old friend, the school where you met, the apartment you once shared.
ideas.think: a school, a university landmark, a first shared apartment, a favorite campus building.
ideas.alt: Friends in graduation gowns gather around a brick model of a campus clock tower.

ideas.title: For someone far from home
verse: Across the country, across an ocean,
for work, for love, for a posting far away —
the smallest details of home grow larger.
paragraphs: Give them a building they know by heart.
ideas.think: a hometown library, a family house abroad, a cherished place of worship, the State House on its hill.
ideas.alt: In a city apartment, a young person smiles at a brick model of the family farmhouse on the windowsill.

ideas.title: For the people you share adventures with
verse: The cabin you return to every summer.
The lighthouse from that unforgettable trip — Beavertail, perhaps, in the wind.
The little hotel everyone still talks about.
paragraphs: A reminder of time well spent, and a reason to plan the next one.
ideas.think: a lakeside cottage, a mountain lodge, a beach house, a favorite landmark.
ideas.alt: Two hikers admire a brick model of a lakeside cabin, with mountains behind them.

ideas.title: For a business anniversary or grand opening
ideas.line: The doors where it all began.
verse: The first day the sign went up.
Ten years of regulars. Twenty-five of the family name over the door.
paragraphs: From family and friends on opening day, or from staff, customers and neighbors when the anniversary comes round: the place itself, for the counter or the window, where everyone who comes in can see it.
ideas.think: a first storefront, a family business, a new restaurant, a new office, a workshop or a farm stand.
ideas.alt: On opening day, a shop owner cuts the ribbon as a friend holds out a brick model of the same corner shop, and neighbors cheer.

ideas.title: From real estate agents
ideas.line: A closing gift they will keep.
verse: For the buyers, the house they have just been handed the keys to.
For the sellers, the home they are saying goodbye to.
paragraphs: Either way, it says you understood what the move meant.

ideas.think: a first home, a forever home, a family home passing to new owners.
ideas.alt: On the front steps, an estate agent hands new owners a brick model of their house, tied with a bow.

ideas.title: From builders and architects
ideas.line: Hand over the keys, and the house in miniature.
verse: The custom home. The careful restoration.
The building you drew from nothing.
paragraphs: The thank-you a client keeps long after the paperwork is filed.
Ordering for clients? See For business: 10% off from your third set in a year.
ideas.think: a custom home, a restored farmhouse, a new chapel or library.
ideas.alt: An architect and a builder present a brick model of a family's new house on their driveway.

ideas.title: For someone retiring or moving on
verse: The office they are leaving. The classroom where they taught.
The fire station they answered calls from.
The corner restaurant that became a neighborhood’s kitchen.
paragraphs: A gift from colleagues, customers or family, for the years someone gave to a place: on the last day before retiring, or when they move on to a new job or a new city.
ideas.think: a long-time workplace, the office they are leaving, a school, a fire station, a family business.
ideas.alt: Colleagues applaud as a colleague receives a brick model of the shop where they worked for years.

ideas.title: For churches, schools and clubs
ideas.line: A building the whole community knows.
verse: A centenary. A new building.
A farewell to an old one.
paragraphs: A model can mark the day, thank someone who served for years, or be the prize everyone hopes to carry home from the fundraiser.
ideas.think: a parish church, a school’s oldest building, a clubhouse, a town library.
ideas.alt: A community gathers in a village hall around a brick model of a white church with a steeple.

ideas.title: A place that holds someone you love
verse: Some places keep a person in them —
a porch, a workshop, a kitchen table.
ideas.think: a parent’s home, a grandparent’s workshop, a place where you spent time together.
ideas.alt: By a lamp-lit window at dusk, an older person holds a brick model of a small cottage, beside a framed photograph and a candle.
